newsitem.title: USA: Cyrix sees Q2 lower revs resulting in loss.
newsitem.headline: Cyrix sees Q2 lower revs resulting in loss.

text.p: Cyrix Corp said Monday that it expects a revenue shortfall to produce a loss in the second quarter.

The microprocessor company said it expects revenues to be "significantly below" the $75.6 million reported in the first quarter this year, but "much stronger" than revenues for the second quarter of 1996.

The company said it will not neet forecasts of revenues flat to slightly up versus the first quarter chiefly due to weak overall demand and significant pricing pressure on the company's non-MMX(TM) 6x86(TM) processor product.

Cyrix, a leading supplier of high-performance processors used in personal computers, said it expects to be around the break-even point for the first half of 1997 versus the large loss posted in the same period last year.
Jay Swent, Cyrix's chief financial officer, said the company was "disappointed" that it will not reach its profit goal in the second quarter.

He noted, however, that during the second quarter Cyrix introduced and shipped more than 35,000 MMX-enhanced 6x86MX processors and that market acceptance of its MediaGX processor continued to meet expectations.
For the second quarter ended June 30, 1996, Cyrix reported a net loss of $16.422 million or $0.81 per share after an extraordinary charge of $0.05 per share, on revenues of $25.1 million.
"Looking forward, our current product lineup positions us well to drive both revenue and profit performance in the second half of 1997," he said.
The outlook from Cyrix comes more than a month after rival chipmaker, Intel Corp, issued a similar warning.

In May, Intel, the world's largest microprocessor maker, said its second quarter results would be hurt by weaker demand for some of its older products, particularly in Europe. The company, which did not provide specifics, said revenues for the three months ended in June would be as much as 10 percent below the $6.4 billion reported in the first quarter.
